requirements.note: The 'Latest' list shows all 420 episodes newest first. Each row shows show, title, full date, minutes and an Unplayed/Played toggle label.
A system 'Unplayed Only' switch filters the list (count line updates). The switch state also persists across relaunch.
The Shows tab lists the 12 shows with episode and unplayed counts. Tapping one pushes that show's episode list with a count header.

The detail screen has show, title, date · length, status, summary, a Play button that becomes 'Playing · Pause' plus a 'Playing' label, and marks the episode played. It also has Add to Up Next and Mark as Played/Unplayed.
Every row has inline 'Unplayed/Played' and '+ Up Next' buttons that work without opening the episode. There are no swipe actions.
Rows can be added from the list or the detail screen. Up Next reorders by dragging the grip. In Edit mode each row gets Earlier/Later/Remove buttons, and Remove works.
Played state, Up Next contents and order, and even the filter switch survived relaunch.

bugs: At the largest text size the Shows rows break inside words: 'Com-mon Groun/d', '35 episode/s · 22 un-played'.
When the large title collapses, the inline 'Latest' title sits directly on top of row text ('Up Next' / 'Unplayed' labels) with no bar background, so the two overlap and are hard to read.
After an episode is added, its 'Queued' / 'Added to Up Next' button is disabled, so it can't be taken back out of the queue from the list or the detail screen.
tells: No swipe actions anywhere: no leading/trailing swipe to mark played or queue on episode rows, and no swipe-to-delete in Up Next.
Each row carries a second line of inline text buttons (○ Unplayed, + Up Next), making rows about 125pt tall and reading like a web card instead of an iOS list cell.
Up Next edit mode is hand-built: text 'Earlier / Later / Remove' buttons under each row instead of the red minus/delete control and system reorder.
The Up Next list has no separators and no grouping, and looks like a plain web list.
Rows are exposed as 'Link' elements, and the detail title is split into separate per-word text runs, which feels web-like.
Shows uses two-letter initials tiles ('CG', 'DW') as artwork, which looks generic.
Played rows aren't visually de-emphasised; only the small toggle label changes.
A.scroll: The 420-row list scrolls smoothly, with no blank or popping rows when flinging, a normal bounce at the top, and the position kept after visiting an episode. The collapsed title overlaps content as it scrolls under.

requirements.note: The Episodes list shows all 420 newest first. Each row has artwork, show, title, date · minutes and a red 'Unplayed' dot or grey 'Played' check.
An 'All episodes / Unplayed' segmented control filters the list (header count goes from 420 to 293). At the largest text it adapts into a switch.
The Shows tab lists 12 shows with artwork, episode count and unplayed count. Tapping one pushes that show's episodes.

The detail screen has artwork, show, title, date · length, status, summary, and a Play episode button that becomes Pause with 'Playing · Preview mode, no audio'. It marks the episode played and shows a Now Playing mini bar.
Swipe left gives 'Mark played' (full swipe works) and swipe right gives 'Up Next'. The ⋯ menu offers Mark as Played/Unplayed and Add to Up Next.
Rows are added via swipe, menu or the detail button. Up Next has system Edit mode with red delete controls and reorder handles, and dragging reorders. Swipe shows Remove.
Played state, queue contents, queue order and removals all survived relaunch.

bugs: The Up Next summary reads '1 episodes · 42 min' (wrong plural).
The 'Weekend Atlas' artwork breaks the word mid-word as 'WEEKEN / D / ATLAS'.
A full swipe left in Up Next triggers 'Mark played' (the outer action) rather than Remove, even though the header says 'Swipe left to remove'.
tells: Heavily branded custom styling: a 'PODCASTS' pill in the nav bar, serif taglines ('A little curiosity. A lot to discover.'), warm cream background and spaced-caps section headers. It is attractive but clearly a designed theme, not stock iOS.
Rows have both a disclosure chevron and a separate ⋯ button next to each other.
There is a large empty gap between the segmented control and the 'LATEST EPISODES' header.
There are two search affordances: a nav-bar search button and a pull-down search field.
The Now Playing bar is a custom opaque strip above the tab bar, not the system tab bar accessory.
At the largest text size, the sticky section header text ('420 episodes') overlaps the row title beneath it.
B.scroll: The long list scrolls smoothly, with sticky blurred section headers, no blank or late-popping rows when flinging, a natural pull-past-top that reveals search, and the position kept after visiting an episode.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist state, but B does it the iOS way: native swipe actions, context menus, a system edit-mode Up Next with delete controls, and layouts that reflow cleanly at the largest text size. A relies on inline web-like buttons, a hand-built Earlier/Later/Remove edit mode with no swipe actions, a collapsed title that overlaps content, and mid-word breaks at large text. B's flaws are small (a pluralisation slip, one artwork word break).
